title: Two tested retrograde fits of TYC 9179-1083-1 have larger errors than the published prograde fit
abstract: We test two retrograde starting states for the published joint timing and velocity solution of TYC 9179-1083-1. We use the same 153 eclipse times, eight velocities, geometry constraints and Newtonian model. The reproduced prograde loss is 140.51. Reversal of the outer angular momentum gives a local fit with loss 713.36 and reaches the adopted tertiary mass limit of 3.98 solar masses. A node-shift fit is much worse. Raising all upper mass limits to 31.62 solar masses lowers the reversal loss to 560.87, still above the prograde result, and reaches a mass boundary again. Without shape constraints, the reversal start moves to a prograde state at 51.32 degrees and loss 140.57, then reaches the evaluation limit. These tests strengthen the prograde interpretation within the tested local searches. They do not exclude all retrograde orbits or give calibrated branch probabilities. No new observations are used. We preserve code, alternative fitted states, source hashes and numerical checks. External measurement tables remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Tested local fits: weighted loss, final mutual inclination and masses. Adopted geometry weights and local searches prevent a global probability claim.
